title: GPU capacity incident data pull & analysis sheet - March 2026
body:
Purpose:
This sheet is a lightweight data-pull spec + scratchpad to support the March 9-10 GPU capacity incident (incident INF-987). The goal: produce reproducible queries and a summary table for saturation, queueing, and throttle signals across regions and instance families so SRE/infra can finalize numbers for the postmortem.
body_2:
How to use:
- Run the SQL snippets below in bigquery-project:redwood-telemetry.jobs (or adapt for internal Clickhouse)
- Collect 1-hour rolling windows and 5m/1m granular samples as noted
- Paste sample output rows into the "SAMPLE_OUTPUT_CSV" section and attach as CSV to the postmortem Confluence page.
- Notes and quick findings go in the "Summary notes" section at the bottom.
query_snippets:
-- 1) node-level GPU utilization (5m avg) over window
SELECT region, gpu_type, node_id, window_start, AVG(gpu_util_percent) as avg_gpu_util
FROM `redwood-telemetry.cluster.node_gpu_metrics`
WHERE window_start BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-03-09T00:00:00Z') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-03-10T23:59:59Z')
GROUP BY region, gpu_type, node_id, window_start
ORDER BY region, avg_gpu_util DESC
LIMIT 1000;

-- 2) queue depth and avg wait time per model route (1m buckets)
SELECT route, region, bucket_start, SUM(queue_depth) as queued, AVG(wait_ms) as avg_wait_ms
FROM `redwood-telemetry.request.queue_stats_1m`
WHERE bucket_start BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-03-09') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-03-10')
AND route LIKE '%/models/%'
GROUP BY route, region, bucket_start
ORDER BY queued DESC
LIMIT 500;

-- 3) throttle events by reason (throttle_count, reason tag)
SELECT region, gpu_family, throttle_reason, COUNT(1) as throttle_events, SUM(throttled_tokens) as tokens_throttled
FROM `redwood-telemetry.infra.throttle_events`
WHERE event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-03-09') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-03-10')
GROUP BY region, gpu_family, throttle_reason
ORDER BY throttle_events DESC;

-- 4) correlate capacity pressure with autoscaler actions
SELECT event_time, region, pool_id, metric, value, autoscaler_action, target_replicas
FROM `redwood-telemetry.autoscaler.actions` a
JOIN `redwood-telemetry.cluster.metrics_1m` m ON a.pool_id = m.pool_id AND ABS(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(a.event_time, m.bucket_start, SECOND)) < 60
WHERE a.event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-03-09') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-03-10')
ORDER BY event_time;

-- 5) request-level tail latency for throttled requests (sampled)
SELECT request_id, route, region, gpu_type, is_throttled, throttle_reason, total_latency_ms
FROM `redwood-telemetry.requests.requests_sampled`
WHERE is_throttled = TRUE AND request_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-03-09') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-03-10')
LIMIT 200;
columns_definitions:
region: cloud region
gpu_type: instance family / accelerator
node_id: internal node identifier
window_start: start of sample window (5m/1m)
avg_gpu_util: average GPU utilization percent
queued: number of requests waiting in scheduler queue
avg_wait_ms: average queue wait in ms
throttle_events: number of throttle events recorded
throttled_tokens: tokens impacted by throttles
quick_checks:
Checklist for data pulls:
- Confirm timezone is UTC for all timestamps
- Use 5m buckets for node-level utilization and 1m for request queueing where possible
- Pull both raw events and aggregated windows to validate aggregation logic
- Cross-check throttle counts against billing-metering logs (billing:gpu_throttle_events)
- Snapshot active deployments (deploy metadata table) for routes that hit throttles
initial_findings:
Preliminary observations (scratch):
- us-west1 A100 pool showed sustained >95% avg for 30+ minutes during incident spike (approx 14:00-14:40 UTC)
- Queue depth for /models/seq2seq-heavy route spiked to 800+ queued requests in 1m buckets before throttles triggered
- Throttle_reason tag 'capacity_saturated' accounts for ~83% of recorded throttle events; other reasons were 'policy_rate_limit' and 'per-user_limit'
- Autoscaler reacted with +20 nodes in us-west1 after ~12 minutes; observed delayed provisioning due to GPU image pull backoff on some hosts (see linked GH PR below)
open_questions:
- Was any workload colocated with background batch jobs that caused ephemeral IO pressure? (check batch-job-runlog-2026-03-09)
- Did preemptible pools on us-east1 contribute by auto-evicting capacity?
- Are there specific model versions that correlate with longer KV-cache startup times?
recommended_next_steps:
Short-term:
- Backfill 1-minute samples for top-5 impacted routes and attach CSV to Confluence
- Run node-level GPU memory pressure query and correlate with image-pull errors in node kubelet logs
- Add an alert to detect sustained avg_gpu_util > 90% for 10m per pool (sensitivity tweak)
Medium-term:
- Evaluate burst buffer pools (warm spare nodes) for A100 in us-west1
- Investigate faster node image caching, pre-pulled images for canary kernels
- Postmortem action: lock a new autoscaler cooldown of 5m to avoid oscillation
notes_for_author: This is a working sheet. Keep it minimal, paste query outputs and annotate rows. Replace SAMPLE_OUTPUT_CSV with full CSV export where possible. For final postmortem, convert the summary section into Confluence-friendly bullets and attach CSVs and dashboards.
